# `vox-plugin-host`

**Crate:** `vox-plugin-host` · **Version:** `0.6.0` · **Target:** Library (`lib.rs`)

Vox host-side plugin discovery, loading, and registry.

## Crate Overview

Vox plugin host: discovery, loading, registry.

See: docs/src/architecture/plugin-system-redesign-2026.md
Spec §4.2(d): a plugin whose manifest `version` disagrees with the
running core's own `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` must be refused before any
attempt to resolve or dlopen its dylib.

### Functions

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| `resolve_plugins_root` | Resolve the plugin install root, respecting `$VOX_PLUGINS_DIR` if set. Falls back to the platform's local data directory under `vox/plugins`. |
| `format_install_hint` | Format the canonical multi-line install hint for a missing plugin.  Always includes the catalog command (`vox plugin install <id>`). When the caller is running from a Vox workspace checkout that contains the plugin source under `crates/vox-plugin-<id>/`, also appends the local-path variant so contributors get a copy-pasteable command pointing at their own checkout (no GitHub fetch needed).  Optionally appends a "Build with cargo:" line when the caller knows the plugin is enabled behind a cargo feature flag on a vox crate (e.g. vox-ml-cli's `gpu` / `mens-candle-cuda`). Pass `Some(cargo_hint)` with the command body — `cargo build -p vox-ml-cli --release --features ...`. |
| `workspace_local_plugin_source` | Detect the in-tree source directory for a plugin id when running from a Vox workspace checkout. Used by `load_code_plugin` to make the "plugin not installed" error message actionable for contributors and by `vox plugin install <id>` (catalog path) to prefer the local checkout over fetching a release tarball.  Walks up from CWD looking for a `crates/vox-plugin-<id>/Plugin.toml`. Returns `Some(path-to-crate-dir)` on the first hit, `None` otherwise. Honors `VOX_WORKSPACE_ROOT` as an explicit override. |
| `current_target_triple_key` | Return the target-triple key used in `[plugin.payload.artifacts]` for the current build.  The format is `"<os>-<arch>"` where `os` is `"windows"`, `"linux"`, or `"macos"` and `arch` is `"x86_64"` or `"aarch64"`.  This matches the keys emitted by the Plugin.toml generator and by `vox plugin install`. |
| `load_code_plugin_by_id` | Convenience wrapper: discover the plugin install root, build the registry, and load a code plugin by id in a single call.  For one-off dispatches from async contexts, wrap in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. |
| `load_code_plugin` | Discover the given plugin in `registry`, resolve the dylib path for the current target triple, and load it via [`Loader`].  This is the preferred one-shot entry point for code-payload plugins.  Callers can then call `.plugin.as_ml_backend()` (or the relevant extension point accessor) on the returned [`LoadedCodePlugin`]. |
| `cached_code_plugin` | Cached singleton: load a code plugin once and reuse the handle process-wide. First call: discover + dlopen (tens of ms). Subsequent calls: O(1) HashMap lookup.  The plugin is leaked for the process lifetime (`Box::leak`) — code plugins are designed to never unload while the host is running. Designed for plugins called repeatedly (browser, mesh, ml backends). |
